import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Jaeger's Petersen-coloring conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Petersen graph § Petersen coloring conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petersen_graph%23Petersen_coloring_conjecture)
- [Ja88] Jaeger, F., *Nowhere-zero flow problems*. In: Selected Topics in Graph Theory 3,
  Academic Press (1988), 71--95.
- [DNR07] DeVos, M., Nešetřil, J., Raspaud, A., *On edge-maps whose inverse preserves flows or
  tensions*. In: Graph Theory in Paris, Trends in Mathematics, Birkhäuser (2007), 109--138.

A *cycle* of a graph $G$, in the sense of the cycle space of $G$, is a set of edges of $G$ that
meets every vertex of $G$ an even number of times; that is, the edge set of an Eulerian subgraph
of $G$. A map from the edges of $G$ to the edges of $H$ is *cycle-continuous* if the preimage of
every cycle of $H$ is a cycle of $G$. Jaeger's Petersen-coloring conjecture asserts that every
bridgeless cubic graph has a cycle-continuous mapping to the Petersen graph.

The Wikipedia article on the Petersen graph states the conjecture for all bridgeless graphs. The
list entry formalised here poses the cubic case, which is the form in which Jaeger stated it and
to which the general case is known to reduce.
-/

open SimpleGraph

namespace JaegersPetersenColoringConjecture

variable {V W : Type*}

/-- A set `S` of edges of `G` is *even* if every vertex of `G` is incident to an even number of
edges of `S`. These sets are the edge sets of the Eulerian subgraphs of `G`, i.e. the elements of
the cycle space of `G` over $\mathbb{Z}/2$; they are also called the *cycles* of `G`. -/
def IsEvenEdgeSet (G : SimpleGraph V) (S : Set G.edgeSet) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : V, Even {e ∈ S | v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)}.ncard

/-- A map `f` from the edges of `G` to the edges of `H` is *cycle-continuous* if the preimage under
`f` of every cycle (even edge set) of `H` is a cycle of `G`. Here `f` is an arbitrary map between
edge sets; it need not come from a graph homomorphism. -/
def IsCycleContinuous (G : SimpleGraph V) (H : SimpleGraph W) (f : G.edgeSet → H.edgeSet) :
    Prop :=
  ∀ C : Set H.edgeSet, IsEvenEdgeSet H C → IsEvenEdgeSet G (f ⁻¹' C)

/-- The Petersen graph, realised as the Kneser graph $K(5, 2)$: its vertices are the $2$-element
subsets of a $5$-element set, and two vertices are adjacent when they are disjoint. -/
def petersenGraph : SimpleGraph {s : Finset (Fin 5) // s.card = 2} where
  Adj s t := Disjoint s.1 t.1
  symm _ _ h := h.symm
  loopless s h := by
    have := s.2
    dsimp only at h
    rw [disjoint_self, Finset.bot_eq_empty] at h
    simp [h] at this

instance : DecidableRel petersenGraph.Adj :=
  fun s t => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (Disjoint s.1 t.1))

/-- **Jaeger's Petersen-coloring conjecture.** Every bridgeless cubic graph $G$ has a
cycle-continuous mapping to the Petersen graph $P$: there is a map $f \colon E(G) \to E(P)$ such
that for every cycle $C$ of $P$ (a set of edges meeting every vertex of $P$ an even number of
times) the preimage $f^{-1}(C)$ is a cycle of $G$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem jaegers_petersen_coloring_conjecture [Fintype V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hcubic : G.IsRegularOfDegree 3) (hbridgeless : G.IsBridgeless) :
    ∃ f : G.edgeSet → petersenGraph.edgeSet, IsCycleContinuous G petersenGraph f := by
  sorry

/-- The Petersen graph has $10$ vertices. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem card_petersenGraph_vertices : Fintype.card {s : Finset (Fin 5) // s.card = 2} = 10 := by
  rw [Fintype.card_finset_len, Fintype.card_fin]
  rfl

/-- The Petersen graph is cubic. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem petersenGraph_isRegularOfDegree_three : petersenGraph.IsRegularOfDegree 3 := by
  unfold IsRegularOfDegree
  decide

/-- The Petersen graph has $15$ edges. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem petersenGraph_card_edgeFinset : petersenGraph.edgeFinset.card = 15 := by
  decide

/-- The empty set of edges is a cycle of every graph. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isEvenEdgeSet_empty (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsEvenEdgeSet G ∅ := by
  intro v
  simp

/-- The identity map on the edges of a graph is cycle-continuous. -/
@[category API, AMS 5]
theorem isCycleContinuous_id (G : SimpleGraph V) : IsCycleContinuous G G id :=
  fun _ hC => hC

/-- The set of all edges of the Petersen graph is not a cycle, since every vertex has degree $3$. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
theorem not_isEvenEdgeSet_univ_petersenGraph : ¬ IsEvenEdgeSet petersenGraph Set.univ := by
  intro h
  have := h ⟨{0, 1}, rfl⟩
  rw [Set.ncard_eq_toFinset_card'] at this
  revert this
  decide

end JaegersPetersenColoringConjecture

variable {V W : Type*}

/-- A finset `C` of edges of `G` is a *cycle* of `G` in the sense of the cycle space (that is, an
Eulerian subgraph of `G`) if every vertex of `G` lies on an even number of edges of `C`. -/
def IsCycleSpaceElement [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) (C : Finset G.edgeSet) : Prop :=
  ∀ v : V, Even #{e ∈ C | v ∈ e.1}

preimage of every cycle of `H` is a cycle of `G`. -/

    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (H : SimpleGraph W) (f : G.edgeSet → H.edgeSet) : Prop :=
  ∀ C : Finset H.edgeSet, IsCycleSpaceElement H C → IsCycleSpaceElement G {e | f e ∈ C}

subsets of a five-element set, and two vertices are adjacent when they are disjoint. -/

  symm _ _ h := h.symm
  loopless a h := by
    have := a.2
    simp only [Finset.disjoint_self_iff_empty] at h
    simp [h] at this

  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (Disjoint a.1 b.1))

-/

theorem jaegers_petersen_coloring_conjecture [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V)
    [DecidableRel G.Adj] (hcubic : G.IsRegularOfDegree 3) (hbridgeless : G.IsBridgeless) :
    ∃ f : G.edgeSet → petersenGraph.edgeSet, IsCycleContinuous G petersenGraph f := by

modeling_decisions: Graphs are finite simple graphs (`SimpleGraph V` with `[Fintype V]`), per the decomposition table. Jaeger's conjecture is often stated for (bridgeless) multigraphs; the simple cubic form is known to be equivalent, but a reviewer should confirm they are content with excluding cubic multigraphs with parallel edges.

'Cubic' is `G.IsRegularOfDegree 3` (every vertex has degree exactly 3); connectedness is not assumed, per the table. The empty graph satisfies the hypotheses vacuously and the conclusion trivially (any f works, all preimages are ∅), which matches the mathematics.

A cycle of a graph is an element of the Z/2 cycle space: a finset of edges meeting every vertex in an even number of edges (`IsCycleSpaceElement`). Since graphs are simple, 'touching a vertex an even number of times' equals 'an even number of incident edges'. The empty edge set counts as a cycle (as in the cycle space).

A cycle-continuous map is a bare function `f : G.edgeSet → petersenGraph.edgeSet` on edge subtypes (not a graph homomorphism); the preimage of C is `Finset.univ.filter (fun e => f e ∈ C)`. The Petersen graph is realised as the Kneser graph K(5,2) (vertices = 2-subsets of Fin 5, adjacent iff disjoint) rather than an explicit edge list on Fin 10; tests confirm 10 vertices, 3-regularity and 15 edges by `decide`.

/-- The Petersen graph, realised as the Kneser graph $KG(5, 2)$: its vertices are the $10$
two-element subsets of a five-element set, and two of them are adjacent if and only if they are
disjoint. -/
def petersenGraph : SimpleGraph {s : Finset (Fin 5) // s.card = 2} where
  Adj s t := Disjoint s.1 t.1
  symm _ _ h := h.symm
  loopless s h := by
    have hs := s.2
    simp only [Finset.disjoint_self_iff_empty] at h
    simp [h] at hs

instance : DecidableRel petersenGraph.Adj :=
  fun s t => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (Disjoint s.1 t.1))

sense of the cycle space over $\mathbb{Z}/2$) if every vertex of `G` lies on an even number of
edges of `C`. Connectedness is not required. The finiteness assumption on the vertex type makes
`Set.ncard` count the edges of `C` at a vertex correctly. -/

  ∀ v : V, Even {e ∈ C | v ∈ (e : Sym2 V)}.ncard

under `f` of every even subgraph (cycle) of `H` is an even subgraph (cycle) of `G`. No

    (f : G.edgeSet → H.edgeSet) : Prop :=
  ∀ C : Set H.edgeSet, IsEvenSubgraph H C → IsEvenSubgraph G (f ⁻¹' C)
